chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Zakariyya al-Naqqad has been transmitted by me from my father—may Allah have mercy on him—from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Zakariyya al-Naqqad.
And he is Zakariyya ibn Malik al-Ju'fi.

key_terms.أَبِي: my father; an immediate link in the author's sanad/isnad
key_terms.الْجُعَفِيُّ: al-Ju'fi; the tribal attribution identifying Zakariyya ibn Malik
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicating the author's mode of transmission
key_terms.زَكَرِيَّا النَّقَّاضِ: Zakariyya al-Naqqad, the transmitter being identified in this sanad/isnad

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Zakariyya al-Naqqad in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from Zakariyya al-Naqqad in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih. It also identifies Zakariyya al-Naqqad by his personal name and lineage as Zakariyya ibn Malik al-Ju'fi.
